subject: Streamline.ai inference cost validation and next steps
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@streamline.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Jenny Park <jenny.park@streamline.ai>
Date: 2026-07-15T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Quick thanks + a few clarifying Qs from today's call

Mina / team —

Thanks for the walkthrough today. High level — the demo helped clarify latency tradeoffs vs. cost, and we liked the KV cache examples. A couple of follow-ups we wanted captured so we can align internally before next week: 

- Current infra: our stack runs on GCP (a mix of A2s and T4s) with a homegrown batching layer in front of TF-serving.
- Primary pain: token cost is starting to hit our margins as we scale synchronous chat (user sessions ~2–4 turns, avg 120 tokens/response). We have spikes during business hours.
- Open question: is Redwood able to plug into our existing batch queue (RabbitMQ) or do we need to route through Redwood's serving router?
- Quantization: engineering says they'd be open to int8 if quality checks pass.

Can you send a short recap with proposed next steps and what data you need from us for a cost model?

—Ethan

--
Ethan Cole
Head of Platform
Streamline.ai
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@streamline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick thanks + a few clarifying Qs from today's call

Ethan —

Thanks for the concise list. Below is a short recap of the call, our understanding of the pain, success criteria, and immediate next steps. I've looped Ben (solutions) and Monica (CS) for technical follow-up and a cost pilot scope.

Recap / pain points
- Latency-sensitive chat: target P95 < 400ms for single-turn inference at peak load.
- Token costs: current per-1M token run-rate is materially pressuring unit economics as MAU grows.
- Spiky traffic: need predictable behavior during peaks; autoscaling alone isn't fixing cost spikes.

Success criteria for a pilot
- 30–40% reduction in per-token inference cost (through batching + KV caching + quantization) without >5% throughput degradation or visible quality regressions in customer-facing responses.
- Maintain P95 latency <= 500ms for most user flows during business-hours traffic.
- Deployment path that keeps customer data in your VPC (you indicated this matters).

Technical assumptions / constraints we heard
- You're running GCP (A2 + T4) today; in some pockets you can run dedicated instances if needed.
- Existing batching layer: RabbitMQ fronting TF-serving; you prefer minimal changes to your queueing.
- Engineering is open to int8/4-bit quantization if we can validate quality via a held-out eval set.

What we propose (high level)
1) Quick feasibility check (1 week): Redwood engineering will map model compatibility (quantization paths), and confirm whether we can integrate with RabbitMQ via a short adapter (likely lightweight).
2) Cost pilot (3–4 weeks): run a limited pilot using your traffic replay + a sample of live traffic with: continuous batching tuned for your session distribution, prefix KV caching for repeated prompts, and one quantized model variant.
3) Success validation and rollout plan: measure unit cost delta, P95 latency, and a small quality eval (n=500 random sessions) to check for regressions.

Data / artifacts we need from you to size the pilot
- Traffic histogram: per-minute requests over the last 2 weeks (CSV or BigQuery export).
- Sample of 500 anonymized sessions (preserve prompt structure, redact PII).
- Current per-token cost (cloud bill line items or estimated) and baseline latency percentiles.

Immediate next steps (agreed items)
- Streamline: share traffic histogram and 500-session sample by EOD Tue (2026-07-20).
- Redwood: Ben to run a model-compatibility check and outline adapter effort (deliverable: short tech note) by 2026-07-17.
- Redwood: Monica to prepare a one-page pilot SOW draft and a cost model template (attached) for your review.

Attachments: I attached a simple cost-model template and a draft SOW to get the conversation started.

If I've missed anything obvious, call it out — otherwise we'll plan to circle back once we have the traffic export.

Thanks,
Mina
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@streamline.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-16T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streamline.ai inference cost validation and next steps

Ethan —

Quick note on the RabbitMQ question: we can build a thin adapter that consumes from your queue and forwards batched requests into Redwood's serving router while preserving order semantics. The engineering estimate for a minimal adapter (alpha) is ~3–5 engineering days including QA — I can produce a short tech note with callouts (auth, retries, trace headers) by end of day Friday (2026-07-17).

On quantization: preliminary compatibility looks fine for your model family. We'll pin two variants in the pilot: a lightly quantized int8 path and a more aggressive 4-bit path so you can compare quality vs. cost. We'll run the held-out eval (Monica will coordinate) and surface nps/accuracy delta.

Ben
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment stub: adapter-design-notes.md
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@streamline.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jenny Park <jenny.park@streamline.ai>
Date: 2026-07-17T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streamline.ai inference cost validation and next steps

Thanks — this is great and aligns with what I need to take to our CTO. A couple clarifications before I share internally: 

- On KV caching: are you proposing prefix caching for repeated system prompts and embeddings cache for re-ranker flows? We have both patterns in our codebase.
- On the traffic export: we'll push a BigQuery export (shared link) by EOD Tue and include a short README for fields.
- On timeline: if the adapter is 3–5 days and the feasibility check a week, we'd aim to have a beta pilot running by end of July. Does that timeline look realistic on your side?

If so, please proceed with Ben's adapter note and Monica's SOW so I can include them in the packet for our CTO.

—Ethan

--
Ethan Cole
Head of Platform
Streamline.ai
